competitions.result: Semi-final — lost a replay 1–0 to Manchester United at Goodison Park after a 2–2 draw at Maine Road.
Second round — lost 1–0 away to Sheffield United.
First round — lost 2–0 on aggregate to Nottingham Forest, losing 2–0 away and drawing 0–0 at home.
Runners-up — lost 4–3 on aggregate to Anderlecht, losing 3–1 away and winning 2–1 at home.

in.note: June 1978 signing, allocated to the incoming campaign.

overview: Liverpool regained the First Division title with 68 points, eight ahead of Nottingham Forest. Bob Paisley’s side won 30 of their 42 league matches, scored 85 goals and conceded only 16. They were unbeaten at Anfield in the league, where opponents scored just four times.

Kenny Dalglish led the scoring with 25 goals in all competitions and was named the football writers’ Footballer of the Year. David Johnson contributed 18 goals, while Alan Kennedy arrived from Newcastle United. A 7–0 win over Tottenham Hotspur at Anfield was among the season’s outstanding league results.

The cups brought less success. Nottingham Forest ended Liverpool’s European Cup defence in the first round, and Anderlecht won the European Super Cup 4–3 on aggregate. Manchester United beat Liverpool in an FA Cup semi-final replay, while Sheffield United knocked them out of the League Cup in the second round.

events.title: Seven against Tottenham
events.detail: Liverpool beat Tottenham Hotspur 7–0 at Anfield.

events.title: The league campaign completed
events.detail: Liverpool won their final league fixture 3–0 at Leeds United and finished with 68 points.

sources.label: Liverpool FC: Kenny Dalglish
sources.claims: Joined from Celtic in August 1977 for £440,000 after Keegan left for Hamburg; led scoring with 31 goals in his first season including the 1978 European Cup winner; Football Writers’ Footballer of the Year in 1979.

sources.label: Liverpool FC: UEFA Super Cup
sources.claims: First won on 6 December 1977, following 1–1 away and 6–0 home results against Hamburg; McDermott hat-trick. Anderlecht won the following edition 4–3 on aggregate.

researchNotes: The 68 points were earned under two points for a win; they should not be compared directly with modern three-point totals. League totals combine the home and away columns in the RSSSF table.

The December 1978 Super Cup belongs to this campaign. Sheedy’s June 1978 arrival is grouped with 1978–79; McGarvey’s May 1979 signing remains here because the league campaign was still in progress. Emlyn Hughes’s later departure must be considered with the following season.
